NAME: COLUMBIA GULF TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: COLUMBIA GULF TRANSMISSION, LLC, A TC ENERGY COMPANY, OPERATES AND MAINTAINS STANTON COMPRESSOR STATION LOCATED IN STANTON, KENTUCKY. ON SATURDAY NOVEMBER 19TH, 2022 A TC ENERGY CLEANING CONTRACTOR HEARD GAS VENTING INTO THE ATMOSPHERE WHILE PERFORMING THEIR DUTIES AT STANTON COMPRESSOR STATION. THE CONTRACTOR IMMEDIATELY CONTACTED COMPRESSOR STATION PERSONNEL; THE STATION PERSONNEL RESPONDED TO THE GAS RELEASE AT STANTON COMPRESSOR STATION AND ADDRESSED THE UNINTENDED RELEASE OF NATURAL GAS THAT WAS VENTING FROM UNIT 108 BLOWDOWN DISCHARGE STACK. THE STATION PERSONNEL INSPECTED AND SECURED THE AREA TO ENSURE THAT IT WAS SAFE; THEN THEN IDENTIFIED VALVES TO ISOLATE THE GAS LINE. THE LINE WAS ISOLATED AT 14:30 EASTERN TIME. ONCE THE LINE WAS ISOLATED THE STATION OPERATING PERSONNEL BEGAN TROUBLESHOOTING THE ISSUE. ALL ALARMS WERE CLEARED AT THE CONTROL PANEL, FUNCTIONAL TESTS WERE COMPLETED WITH NO NEW ERRORS GENERATED TO ENSURE NORMAL OPERATION OF THE STATION.    PRELIMINARY INVESTIGATION IDENTIFIED THE PROBABLE CAUSE THAT LED TO THIS UNINTENDED RELEASE AT UNIT 108 WAS DUE TO A LOSS OF POWER TO A PROGRAMMABLE LOGIC CONTROLLER (PLC) AND RELAY FAILURE. THE LOSS OF POWER TO THIS PLC CAUSED THE COMPRESSOR UNIT BLOW DOWN VALVE (AOV 8810) TO REMAIN OPEN. THE VALVE REMAINED OPEN FOR 50 MINUTES RESULTING IN AN ESTIMATED TOTAL GAS LOST OF 5,328.8 MCF. THE PRESSURE OF THE LINE AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT WAS 779 LBS.    RELAY K340-2B DID NOT UNLATCH FROM ITS N/C STATE AFTER LOSING ITS POWER OR DE-ENERGIZED STATE TO N/O WHICH WOULD HAVE ALLOWED UNIT SUCTION/DISCHARGE VALVES TO BECOME CLOSED OR INTO A FAIL TO CLOSE/SHUT PHASE PER DESIGN. THIS WOULD HAVE PREVENTED GAS FROM VENTING TO ATMOSPHERE VIA UNIT FOUR INCH BLOWN DOWN SILENCER STACK. WITH POWER RESTORED & RELAY REPLACED, THE REMAINING SECTION OF CIRCUIT WAS TESTED TO MAKE SURE PROPER PANEL FEEDBACK, CONTINUITY TEST TO YARD VALVES COMPONENTS WAS VERIFIED AND SUCCESSFUL.
narrative_clean: columbia gulf transmission, llc, a tc energy company, operates and maintains stanton compressor station located in stanton, kentucky. on saturday november 19th, 2022 a tc energy cleaning contractor heard gas venting into the atmosphere while performing their duties at stanton compressor station. the contractor immediately contacted compressor station personnel; the station personnel responded to the gas release at stanton compressor station and addressed the unintended release of natural gas that was venting from unit 108 blowdown discharge stack. the station personnel inspected and secured the area to ensure that it was safe; then then identified valves to isolate the gas line. the line was isolated at 14:30 eastern time. once the line was isolated the station operating personnel began troubleshooting the issue. all alarms were cleared at the control panel, functional tests were completed with no new errors generated to ensure normal operation of the station. preliminary investigation identified the probable cause that led to this unintended release at unit 108 was due to a loss of power to a programmable logic controller (plc) and relay failure. the loss of power to this plc caused the compressor unit blow down valve (aov 8810) to remain open. the valve remained open for 50 minutes resulting in an estimated total gas lost of 5,328.8 mcf. the pressure of the line at the time of the incident was 779 lbs. relay k340-2b did not unlatch from its n/c state after losing its power or de-energized state to n/o which would have allowed unit suction/discharge valves to become closed or into a fail to close/shut phase per design. this would have prevented gas from venting to atmosphere via unit four inch blown down silencer stack. with power restored & relay replaced, the remaining section of circuit was tested to make sure proper panel feedback, continuity test to yard valves components was verified and successful.

NAME: COLORADO INTERSTATE GAS CO
NARRATIVE: ON 11/18/2022, AT 09:37, A 3 INCH EMERGENCY SHUT DOWN (ESD) VALVE UNINTENTIONALLY OPENED AT THE COLORADO INTERSTATE GAS (CIG), MUDDY GAP COMPRESSORS STATION. AT 22:14, CIG GAS CONTROL CALLED THE FIELD OPERATOR ON DUTY AND COMMUNICATED THAT PRESSURE WAS TRENDING DOWN AND A VENT VALVE MAY BE OPEN AT THE MUDDY GAP COMPRESSOR STATION. THE NRC NOTIFICATION WAS ISSUED, AND THE INTERNAL INVESTIGATION STARTED.     THE INTERNAL INVESTIGATION CONCLUDED THAT THE ESD VALVE SOLENOID FAILED DUE TO AN ACCUMULATION OF WATER AND DEBRIS FROM THE STATION SUPPLY AIR SYSTEM THAT FROZE CAUSING THE VALVE TO OPERATE ABNORMALLY SENDING A PNEUMATIC OPEN SIGNAL TO THE ESD VALVE. IN ADDITION, THE VALVE STATUS WAS NOT IN SCADA AND THE CONTROLLERS DID NOT GET AN ALARM NOTIFYING THEM THAT THE VENT VALVE WAS OPEN.       IN ORDER TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE CIG OPERATIONS CLEANED AND RE-TESTED THE VALVE SOLENOID. OPERATIONS IS REVIEWING PROCESSES AND PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE MEASURES TO VERIFY THAT THE MUDDY GAP CS SUPPLIED AIR SYSTEMS ARE DRY THROUGHOUT THE ENTIRE SYSTEM. IN ADDITION, OPERATIONS ADDED VALVE STATUS PLC LOGIC ALARMS IN SCADA FOR THE MUDDY GAP ESD VALVES.
narrative_clean: on 11/18/2022, at 09:37, a 3 inch emergency shut down (esd) valve unintentionally opened at the colorado interstate gas (cig), muddy gap compressors station. at 22:14, cig gas control called the field operator on duty and communicated that pressure was trending down and a vent valve may be open at the muddy gap compressor station. at 23:30, cig field operator arrived on site and discovered an esd valve was open. the operator closed the valve. the incident was deemed reportable. the nrc notification was issued, and the internal investigation started. the internal investigation concluded that the esd valve solenoid failed due to an accumulation of water and debris from the station supply air system that froze causing the valve to operate abnormally sending a pneumatic open signal to the esd valve. in addition, the valve status was not in scada and the controllers did not get an alarm notifying them that the vent valve was open. in order to prevent reoccurrence cig operations cleaned and re-tested the valve solenoid. operations is reviewing processes and preventive maintenance measures to verify that the muddy gap cs supplied air systems are dry throughout the entire system. in addition, operations added valve status plc logic alarms in scada for the muddy gap esd valves.

NAME: FLORIDA GAS TRANSMISSION CO
NARRATIVE: ON JANUARY 16, 2023, AT APPROXIMATELY 07:00, A FLORIDA GAS TRANSMISSION TECHNICIAN DISCOVERED A COMPRESSOR UNIT VENT VALVE WAS VENTING NATURAL GAS TO ATMOSPHERE AT THE COMPRESSOR STATION 24, NEAR TRENTON, FL. THE TECHNICIAN ISOLATED THE COMPRESSOR AT APPROXIMATELY 0730 HRS. ACCORDING TO COMPANY SCADA, THE VENT VALVE HAD BEGUN VENTING AT APPROXIMATELY 13:00 ON JANUARY 15, 2023, BUT NO OTHER SCADA ALARMS WERE TRIGGERED. THE UNIT WAS SHUT DOWN REMOTELY BY GAS CONTROL AT 11:00 ON JANUARY 15, 2023. THE COMPRESSOR UNIT AUTOMATICALLY VENTS AFTER TWO (2) HOURS OF SHUTDOWN. THE SHUTDOWN AND ALL VALVE POSITIONS INDICATED CLOSURE; THEREFORE, NO ALARMS WERE TRIGGERED.    THE VOLUME RELEASED WAS CALCULATED TO BE APPROXIMATELY 102.6 MMSCF NATURAL GAS. THE DETERMINATION TIME FOR THIS ESTIMATE WAS APPROXIMATELY 14:52 ON JANUARY 16, 2023, WHICH WAS FOLLOWED BY THE NRC NOTIFICATION THAT OCCURRED AT APPROXIMATELY 15:44.    THE CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT WAS LATER CONFIRMED TO BE A SUCTION SIDE ISOLATION VALVE NOT FULLY SEATING AFTER THE COMPRESSOR UNIT WAS SHUTDOWN. SPECIFICALLY, IT APPEARS THAT THE VALVE ACTUATOR MALFUNCTIONED RESULTING IN THE VALVE NOT FULLY SEATING, THEREBY ALLOWING PIPELINE PRESSURE TO BLEED BY INTO THE COMPRESSOR UNIT CAUSING THE NATURAL GAS TO BE VENTED TO ATMOSPHERE. THE SUCTION SIDE VALVE WAS FULLY CLOSED MANUALLY BY THE TECHNICIAN TO STOP FLOW OF GAS THROUGH THE COMPRESSOR. THE LOGIC TO ALLOW MORE TIME FOR VALVE CLOSURE WAS DEVELOPED AND INSTALLED THE DAY OF THE RCFA INVESTIGATION TO PREVENT RECURRENCE.
narrative_clean: on january 16, 2023, at approximately 07:00, a florida gas transmission technician discovered a compressor unit vent valve was venting natural gas to atmosphere at the compressor station 24, near trenton, fl. the technician isolated the compressor at approximately 0730 hrs. according to company scada, the vent valve had begun venting at approximately 13:00 on january 15, 2023, but no other scada alarms were triggered. the unit was shut down remotely by gas control at 11:00 on january 15, 2023. the compressor unit automatically vents after two (2) hours of shutdown. the shutdown and all valve positions indicated closure; therefore, no alarms were triggered. the volume released was calculated to be approximately 102.6 mmscf natural gas. the determination time for this estimate was approximately 14:52 on january 16, 2023, which was followed by the nrc notification that occurred at approximately 15:44. the cause of the incident was later confirmed to be a suction side isolation valve not fully seating after the compressor unit was shutdown. specifically, it appears that the valve actuator malfunctioned resulting in the valve not fully seating, thereby allowing pipeline pressure to bleed by into the compressor unit causing the natural gas to be vented to atmosphere. the suction side valve was fully closed manually by the technician to stop flow of gas through the compressor. the logic to allow more time for valve closure was developed and installed the day of the rcfa investigation to prevent recurrence.

NAME: AGUA TRANQUILLO MIDSTREAM LLC
NARRATIVE: ON OCTOBER 22, 2021, A 3RD PARTY PERSON WAS WORKING AT THEIR COMPANY DOCK FACILITY AND NOTICED A LARGE STREAM OF BUBBLES RISING TO THE WATER SURFACE IN THE NAVIGATION CHANNEL.  THIS THIRD PARTY NOTIFIED LOCAL EMERGENCY OFFICIALS.  COMPANY EMPLOYEES WERE NOTIFIED BY THE LOCAL EMERGENCY OFFICIALS AND RESPONDED TO THE LOCATION. DUE TO THE LOCATION OF THE INCIDENT AND SLIGHT CONCERN FOR IGNITION, THE REMAINING PRESSURE WAS RELIEVED TO ATMOSPHERE, IN A CONTROLLED MANNER, AT THE DOWNSTREAM BLOCK VALVE.  EFFORTS TO INVESTIGATE THE CAUSE OF FAILURE HAS NOT BEEN SUCCESSFUL.  THE INCIDENT LOCATION IS IN A CRITICAL NAVIGATION CHANNEL IN THE CORPUS CHRISTI BAY.  THE CHANNEL IS 50 FEET DEEP TO ACCOMMODATE LARGER TANKER AND LNG VESSELS.  THE U.S. ARMY CORP OF ENGINEERS AND THE LOCAL NAVIGATION AUTHORITY RESTRICTED THE AMOUNT OF TIME DIVERS COULD BE IN CHANNEL INVESTIGATING THE FAILURE.  TO DETERMINATION OF CAUSE OF FAILURE WAS MADE DUE TO THE USACE TIME RESTRICTIONS AND THE EXCESSIVE COST OF INVESTIGATION.  THE USACE AND LOCAL NAVIGATION AUTHORITY IN THE CORPUS CHRISTI BAY IS WORKING TO INCREASE THE OPERATIONAL DEPTHS OF THE SHIPPING LANES IN THE BAY.  AN AGREEMENT HAS BEEN REACHED WITH THE USACE THAT THE PIPELINE OWNERSHIP WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO THE USACE AND THE USACE WILL ABANDONED THE PIPELINE.      A16B. AGUA RESPONSE: AGUA WAS NOT ABLE TO COMPLETE A FULL INVESTIGATION INTO THE INCIDENT. FOR 40 DAYS AGUA TRIED TO LOCATE THE LEAK BUT WERE UNSUCCESSFUL. WE SPENT NEARLY 4 MILLION DOLLARS IN THE PROCESS AND WERE ON THE VERGE OF BEING SUED BY MULTIPLE COMPANIES IN THE LAQUINTA CHANNEL, BECAUSE AGUA WAS INTERRUPTING THEIR BUSINESS OBLIGATIONS.  DURING THE INCIDENT, THE USACE AND POCC WERE PUSHING AGUA TO SHUT IN THE PIPELINES AND REMOVE A SECTION THAT RUNS THROUGH THE CC SHIP CHANNEL. AGUA SURRENDERED THE PIPELINES TO USACE IN 2023. TO DATE, THE USACE HAS ALREADY PIGGED AND REMOVED THE SHIP CHANNEL SECTIONS LEAVING NO WAY TO CONTINUE ANY WORK ON THE REMAINING PIECES OF THE PIPELINES. THEREFORE IT IS UNNECESSARY FOR AGUA TO CREATE A PLAN TO PREVENT RECURRENCE.  AGUA'S CONTRACTOR MR. RICHARD WATSON WITH WHITE MARLIN OPERATING ADVISED THAT REPAIR EQUIPMENT WOULD BEGIN ARRIVING OCTOBER 23, 2021, TO THE BROWNWATER DOCK IN ARANSAS PASS, TX FOR TRANSIT INCIDENT SITE. THE OPERATOR ATTEMPTED TO LOCATE THE FAILED SECTION OF PIPE WITH DIVERS AND A NITROGEN TRUCK LOCATE THE LEAK. THE DIVERS FAILED TO LOCATE THE LOCATION OF THE LEAK. THE OPERATOR'S FINANCIAL DEPARTMENT AND INSURANCE AGENCY ELECTED TO ABANDON THE INVESTIGATION PROJECT DUE TO FINANCIAL CONSTRAINTS.  ON FEB. 25, 2022, THE OPERATOR NOTIFIED MR. NUERNBERG THAT THE CORP OF ENGINEERS IS TO ABANDON THE PIPELINE SYSTEM. IT WAS REPORTED THAT THE CORP OF ENGINEERS IS IN THE PROCESS OF PULLING THE T-4 PERMITS ON THE PIPELINE SYSTEM AND THE CORP OF ENGINEERS WOULD ALSO BE WORKING ON A PLAN TO CUT AND REMOVE THE SECTION OF PIPELINE IN THE SHIP CHANNEL. FURTHER ANALYSIS IS REQUIRED TO SUPPORT CONFIRMATION OF THE PIPE FAILURE MODES IDENTIFIED IN THE FIELD AND IS PRESENTLY UNDERWAY. THE ORIGINAL EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURER HAS BEEN ENGAGED IN THE REVIEW AND REPAIR PLAN AND IS SUPPORTING REVIEW OF THE STRESS ANALYSIS. ENGINEERING SUPPORT HAS BEEN CONTRACTED TO SUPPORT MODEL DEVELOPMENT OF THE SYSTEM AND EXECUTE A PIPE STRESS ANALYSIS. FOLLOWING THE OUTCOME OF THE MODELING AND VALIDATION OF THE FAILURE MODES, ADDITIONAL STEPS MAY BE NECESSARY TO IMPROVE THE INTEGRITY OF THE SYSTEM AND WILL BE IMPLEMENTED ACCORDINGLY. THE TOTAL VOLUME RELEASED THAT DAY WAS 17.76 MMSCF TOTALING BETWEEN TWO PSV'S ON MAINLINE 40 AT THE JL40-47 JUNCTION AND GREEN RIVER METER STATION, BUT BOTH RELEASED GAS DUE TO THE SAME CAUSE. AT THE TIME OF THE INITIAL RELEASE OPERATIONS WAS ON SITE PERFORMING OTHER WORK AT THE JL40-47 JUNCTION.      AT THE TIME OF THE RELEASE THERE WERE TWO COMPRESSOR STATIONS THAT WERE DOWN FOR MAINTENANCE, THIS LEFT ONLY ONE COMPRESSOR STATION AVAILABLE IN THE AREA TO MOVE GAS. AN ISSUE ON THE FUEL CONTROL VALVE WITH THE COMPRESSOR THAT WAS RUNNING CAUSED REPEATED SHUTDOWNS. THESE REPEATED SHUTDOWNS CAUSED GAS TO BACKUP ON THE SYSTEM AND PRESSURES BUILT UP, ULTIMATELY CAUSING THE TWO PSV'S TO LIFT ON THE MAINLINE RESULTING IN THE GAS RELEASE THAT WAS REPORTED. THE FUEL VALVES WERE OPERATED IN SAFE MODE TO SUBVERT A POWERED HOUR LIMITATION SET BY SOLAR TO KEEP FLOW THROUGH ON THE LINE, HOWEVER THEY HAD TO BE RESTARTED EVERY HOUR TO MAINTAIN THIS.

NAME: EQUITRANS MIDSTREAM CORPORATION
NARRATIVE: AT 22:54 ON 7/4/2024, COMPLIANCE RECEIVED A CALL INDICATING THAT GAS WAS LEAKING PAST A CHECK VALVE ON THE DISCHARGE SIDE OF THE COMPRESSOR, WHICH CAUSED A RELIEF VALVE TO GO OFF, AND GAS TO MIGRATE TO A UNIT THAT HAD SHUT DOWN EARLIER IN THE DAY. THAT UNIT WAS SHUT DOWN FOR A DIFFERENT REASON UNRELATED TO THE CAUSE OF THIS INCIDENT. THE SHUT DOWN UNIT HAS A SAFETY FEATURE THAT VENTS ALL GAS THROUGH THE BLOWDOWN STACK. THE VENTING STARTED TO OCCUR AT APPROXIMATELY 4:30 AND STOPPED AT APPROXIMATELY 10:35, RESULTING IN AN APPROXIMATE LOSS OF 7,771 MCF OF GAS LOST (UPDATED FROM 7,500 MCF ON THE NRC REPORTS). WHEN OPERATIONS ARRIVED ON SITE, A BALL VALVE WAS SHUT UPSTREAM OF THE UNIT TO BLOCK ANY MORE GAS FROM BEING VENTED. ON MONDAY, 7/8, OPERATIONS INSPECTED THE CHECK VALVE AND FOUND A TEFLON BOLT STUCK IN THE VALVE. ONCE THE BOLT WAS REMOVED, THE VALVE WAS ABLE TO OPERATE NORMALLY.     THE TEFLON BOLT HOLDS THE COMPRESSOR VALVE CAGES IN THE CYLINDER OF THE COMPRESSOR. THESE BOLTS ARE KEPT IN THE COMPRESSOR PER THE COMPRESSOR MANUFACTURER'S DESIGN. THE BOLTS ARE NOT MEANT TO BE REMOVED UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE. GOING FORWARD, THE TECHNICIANS WILL INSPECT THE BOLTS DURING COMPRESSOR MAINTENANCE FOR SECURE FIT, WEAR, AND DAMAGE. THEY WILL BE REPLACED AS NEEDED. THE COMPANY WILL REVIEW ITS PROCEDURES TO DETERMINE IF ANY CHANGES ARE NECESSARY.

NAME: HARDY STORAGE
NARRATIVE: ON JANUARY 19, 2025, TC ENERGY CONFIRMED AN UNINTENTIONAL GAS RELEASE AT THE HARDY COMPRESSOR STATION IN HARDY COUNTY, WEST VIRGINIA, AFTER A LANDOWNERS REPORTED A POTENTIAL ISSUE. UPON ARRIVAL, OPERATIONS PERSONNEL OBSERVED NATURAL GAS BEING RELEASED TO THE ATMOSPHERE AND CONFIRMED THE FAILURE AT 1906 EST. THE FAILURE WAS TRACED TO ESD BLOW-OFF VALVE C182-135, WHICH OPENED OUT OF SEQUENCE DUE TO BELOW FREEZING AMBIENT ATMOSPHERIC TEMPERATURES CAUSING A PRESSURE DROP IN ONE OF THE COMPONENTS OF THE ESD SYSTEM. OPERATIONS DISCONNECTED TUBING TO COMPONENT TO ESD SYSTEM AND BLEW OUT THE LINE TO REMOVE FROZEN CONDENSATION FROM THE TUBING. AFTERWARDS OPERATIONS RECONNECTED THE TUBING AND RESTORED THE C182-135 VALVE BACK TO SERVICE. TC ENERGY WILL ASSESS MITIGATION MEASURES TO PREVENT RECURRENCE.
narrative_clean: on january 19, 2025, tc energy confirmed an unintentional gas release at the hardy compressor station in hardy county, west virginia, after a landowners reported a potential issue. upon arrival, operations personnel observed natural gas being released to the atmosphere and confirmed the failure at 1906 est. the failure was traced to esd blow-off valve c182-135, which opened out of sequence due to below freezing ambient atmospheric temperatures causing a pressure drop in one of the components of the esd system. operations disconnected tubing to component to esd system and blew out the line to remove frozen condensation from the tubing. afterwards operations reconnected the tubing and restored the c182-135 valve back to service. tc energy will assess mitigation measures to prevent recurrence.

NAME: GULF RUN TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: ON 2/15/2025 THE VERNON COMPRESSOR STATION LOST COMMERCIAL POWER. IN ADDITION, THE EMERGENCY GENERATOR FAILED TO START, AND THE STATION BATTERY UPS SYSTEM FAILED TO SWITCH TO BATTERY BACKUP. THE UPS IS USED TO MAINTAIN POWER TO STATION NETWORKS, PLC'S, AND HMIS FOR SHORT PERIODS OF TIME UNTIL EITHER COMMERCIAL OR EMERGENCY GENERATOR POWER BECOMES AVAILABLE. WITH NO POWER, A NORMAL STOP COMMAND WAS ISSUED TO ALL THREE STATION TURBINES. THE TURBINES STOPPED, THE UNIT BLOWDOWN VALVES OPENED, AND THE FUEL SUPPLY VALVES CLOSED. THE STATION ESD BLOWDOWN VALVES ARE DESIGNED TO DEFAULT TO THE FAIL-OPEN POSITION AND MUST BE MANUALLY RESET. STATION BLOWDOWN VALVES WERE SET TO OPEN AT 55PSI. THE ESD PRESSURE DROPPED BELOW 50PSI, WHICH ACTIVATED THE VALVES, AND BEGAN RELIEVING THE STATION PRESSURE. TECHNICIANS ARRIVED ON LOCATION AND BLOCKED IN THE STATION DURING THE BLOWDOWN PROCESS, PRIOR TO A FULL STATION BLOWDOWN. CORRECTIVE ACTIONS TAKEN TO HAVE THE STATION BACK ONLINE BY 2/16/2025 AT 4:00AM.     REMEDIAL ACTIONS TAKEN, SMALL LEAK WAS FOUND ON THE ESD SYSTEM. THE ESD PILOTS ON BLOWDOWN VALVES WERE RESET TO 30PSI AND THE SIDE GATE ESD PILOTS WERE REST TO 45PSI. ORIGINAL CONSTRUCTION DESIGN WAS CHANGED FROM UTILIZING ESD GAS AS PILOT PRESSURE TO POWER GAS. ALL REGULATORS WERE TESTED AND TRENDED TO ENSURE PROPER OPERATION. GENERATOR LOGIC ISSUES WERE IDENTIFIED AND CORRECTED, THEN MULTIPLE SIMULATED POWER LOSS SCENARIOS WERE RUN TO ENSURE THE GENERATOR TRANSFERRED PROPERLY AND CARRIED THE STATION LOAD.
narrative_clean: on 2/15/2025 the vernon compressor station lost commercial power. in addition, the emergency generator failed to start, and the station battery ups system failed to switch to battery backup. the ups is used to maintain power to station networks, plc's, and hmis for short periods of time until either commercial or emergency generator power becomes available. with no power, a normal stop command was issued to all three station turbines. the turbines stopped, the unit blowdown valves opened, and the fuel supply valves closed. the station esd blowdown valves are designed to default to the fail-open position and must be manually reset. station blowdown valves were set to open at 55psi. the esd pressure dropped below 50psi, which activated the valves, and began relieving the station pressure. technicians arrived on location and blocked in the station during the blowdown process, prior to a full station blowdown. corrective actions taken to have the station back online by 2/16/2025 at 4:00am. remedial actions taken, small leak was found on the esd system. the esd pilots on blowdown valves were reset to 30psi and the side gate esd pilots were rest to 45psi. original construction design was changed from utilizing esd gas as pilot pressure to power gas. all regulators were tested and trended to ensure proper operation. generator logic issues were identified and corrected, then multiple simulated power loss scenarios were run to ensure the generator transferred properly and carried the station load.

NAME: UGI ENERGY SERVICES
NARRATIVE: ON MARCH 20, 2025, COMPRESSOR #2 WAS PLACED IN MAINTENANCE MODE FOR TROUBLESHOOTING AN ESD VENT VALVE STATUS ISSUE. LOOSE TERMINALS IN THE ACTUATOR CONTROL BOARD WERE IDENTIFIED AND REPAIRED. HOWEVER, MAINTENANCE MODE WAS ACCIDENTALLY LEFT ACTIVE OVERNIGHT.    THE MAINTENANCE MODE SHOULD HAVE TRIGGERED LOCAL ALARMS AND SMS NOTIFICATIONS AT 2, 12, AND 24 HOURS, BUT SMS ALERTS FAILED TO GENERATE. OPERATORS MISSED THE MAINTENANCE STATUS ON LOCAL SCADA DISPLAYS THE MORNING OF MARCH 21.    AT 12:24 ON MARCH 21, COMPRESSOR #2 SUCTION AND DISCHARGE BLOCK VALVES UNEXPECTEDLY CLOSED. NORMALLY THIS WOULD TRIGGER UNIT SHUTDOWN, BUT MAINTENANCE MODE BLOCKED ALL SHUTDOWN SIGNALS, FORCING THE COMPRESSOR TO RUN WITH CLOSED VALVES UNTIL 13:05 WHEN OPERATORS RECEIVED A LOSS OF RUN STATUS ALARM.    PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT 13:14 AND ASSESSED DAMAGE. DURING INSPECTION, A SMALL OIL FIRE WAS DETECTED BY THE SAFETY SYSTEM, CAUSING STATION ESD AT 13:23. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL IMMEDIATELY EXTINGUISHED THE FIRE.    POST-INCIDENT SCADA ANALYSIS REVEALED BOTH VALVES OPENED WITHOUT COMMAND AFTER THE COMPRESSOR STOPPED. THE ENGINE CONTROL PANEL INDICATED SHUTDOWN DUE TO MECHANICAL OVERLOAD.    THE VALVE CLOSURE CAUSED CATASTROPHIC MECHANICAL FAILURE REQUIRING COMPLETE REPLACEMENT OF FRAME, CRANKCASE, CRANKSHAFT, CYLINDERS, AND ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS. THE MAINTENANCE MODE CAPABILITY HAS BEEN ELIMINATED FROM STATION PLC PROGRAMMING.    ROOT CAUSE WAS IDENTIFIED AS MALFUNCTION IN VALVE CONTROL CIRCUITRY, HARDWARE, WIRING, AND CONNECTIONS BETWEEN PLC AND VALVE ACTUATORS. DUE TO THE INTERMITTENT NATURE, SPECIFIC COMPONENT ISOLATION WAS IMPOSSIBLE DURING ONLINE OPERATION. INVESTIGATION ELIMINATED PLC PROGRAMMING AND HARDWARE, NARROWING THE FAULT TO PHYSICAL CONNECTIONS INCLUDING I/O BOARDS, CABINET CONNECTIONS, AND FIELD WIRING. HISTORICAL REVIEW REVEALED SIMILAR VALVE CLOSURES PREVIOUSLY MISDIAGNOSED AS PNEUMATIC ISSUES.    PRIOR TO RESTART, ALL PLC I/O BOARDS FOR BLOCK VALVE CONTROL WERE REPLACED, WIRING CONTINUITY VERIFIED, AND ACTUATOR TERMINATIONS INSPECTED. SINCE RETURNING TO SERVICE APRIL 29, 2025, NO UNEXPECTED VALVE POSITION CHANGES OCCURRED. COMBINED WITH REMOVAL OF PROBLEMATIC MAINTENANCE FUNCTIONS AND NEW MAINTENANCE MODE SAFEGUARDS, WE ARE CONFIDENT THE ROOT CAUSE IS RESOLVED AND SIMILAR ELECTRICAL FAILURES WOULD NOT RESULT IN THE SAME INCIDENT TYPE.
narrative_clean: on march 20, 2025, compressor #2 was placed in maintenance mode for troubleshooting an esd vent valve status issue. loose terminals in the actuator control board were identified and repaired. however, maintenance mode was accidentally left active overnight. the maintenance mode should have triggered local alarms and sms notifications at 2, 12, and 24 hours, but sms alerts failed to generate. operators missed the maintenance status on local scada displays the morning of march 21. at 12:24 on march 21, compressor #2 suction and discharge block valves unexpectedly closed. normally this would trigger unit shutdown, but maintenance mode blocked all shutdown signals, forcing the compressor to run with closed valves until 13:05 when operators received a loss of run status alarm. personnel arrived at 13:14 and assessed damage. during inspection, a small oil fire was detected by the safety system, causing station esd at 13:23. operations personnel immediately extinguished the fire. post-incident scada analysis revealed both valves opened without command after the compressor stopped. the engine control panel indicated shutdown due to mechanical overload. the valve closure caused catastrophic mechanical failure requiring complete replacement of frame, crankcase, crankshaft, cylinders, and associated components. the maintenance mode capability has been eliminated from station plc programming. root cause was identified as malfunction in valve control circuitry, hardware, wiring, and connections between plc and valve actuators. due to the intermittent nature, specific component isolation was impossible during online operation. investigation eliminated plc programming and hardware, narrowing the fault to physical connections including i/o boards, cabinet connections, and field wiring. historical review revealed similar valve closures previously misdiagnosed as pneumatic issues. prior to restart, all plc i/o boards for block valve control were replaced, wiring continuity verified, and actuator terminations inspected. since returning to service april 29, 2025, no unexpected valve position changes occurred. combined with removal of problematic maintenance functions and new maintenance mode safeguards, we are confident the root cause is resolved and similar electrical failures would not result in the same incident type.

CAUSE_DETAILS: DEFECTIVE OR LOOSE TUBING OR FITTING
NARRATIVE: ON AUGUST 28, 2025, THERE WAS A RELEASE OF GAS AT THE SNAPPING TURTLE COMPRESSOR STATION LOCATED IN WIND RIDGE, PA WHICH IS OWNED AND OPERATED BY EQT PRODUCTION. CHIEF INSPECTOR TROY LEEK CALLED THE EQT ENVIRONMENTAL, HEALTH, & SAFETY (EHS) HOTLINE TO REPORT A GAS RELEASE AT THE SNAPPING TURTLE COMPRESSOR STATION. UPON ARRIVAL TO THE LOCATION, HE OBSERVED THE RICHHILL TOWNSHIP FIRE DEPARTMENT (WHO HAD BEEN DISPATCHED TO THE LOCATION UPON COMMUNITY NOTIFICATION), STAGED ~150' AWAY ON THE SHARED ACCESS ROAD. ALL CONTRACT PERSONNEL WERE MUSTERED OUTSIDE OF THE GATE. THE OPERATIONS SUPERVISOR (JOHN MINCIN) WAS NOTIFIED. GAS CONTROL WAS CONTACTED TO INITIATE A REMOTE SHUT IN OF COMPRESSOR UNIT #3, AND OPERATIONS PERSONNEL WERE DISPATCHED TO THE SITE. UPON EXAMINATION, THERE WAS A TUBING FAILURE ON A RELIEF VALVE INSIDE THE STATION.     UPON EVALUATION, OPERATIONS DETERMINED THAT NO OVERPRESSURE EVENT OCCURRED. PRESSURE WAS ~917PSI WHEN THE PRV LIFTED. IT WAS NOTED THAT THE NUT AND FERRULE OF THE 1/8" STAINLESS STEEL TUBING BROKE AT THE PILOT WHICH, BY DESIGN, CAUSED A LOSS OF PRESSURE TO THE MAIN VALVE DOME THUS TRIGGERING A FAIL-OPEN CONDITION (CAUSED THE RELIEF VALVE TO LIFT). THE SUSPECTED FAILURE IS EXCESSIVE VIBRATION, SO NEW TUBING WAS INSTALLED IN A CONFIGURATION THAT ALLEVIATED THE VIBRATION ISSUE. EQT PRODUCTION EXAMINED OTHER STATIONS WITH SIMILAR TUBING CONFIGURATIONS AS THE FAILED TUBING AND FOUND THEM TO BE FULLY OPERATIONAL FOR MANY YEARS AND WITHOUT VIBRATION ISSUES. EQT PRODUCTION BELIEVES THAT THIS WAS AN ISOLATED EVENT AND PARTICULAR TO THE RELIEF VALVE TUBING AT THIS SPECIFIC RELIEF VALVE AT SNAPPING TURTLE COMPRESSOR STATION.
narrative_clean: on august 28, 2025, there was a release of gas at the snapping turtle compressor station located in wind ridge, pa which is owned and operated by eqt production. chief inspector troy leek called the eqt environmental, health, & safety (ehs) hotline to report a gas release at the snapping turtle compressor station. upon arrival to the location, he observed the richhill township fire department (who had been dispatched to the location upon community notification), staged ~150' away on the shared access road. all contract personnel were mustered outside of the gate. the operations supervisor (john mincin) was notified. gas control was contacted to initiate a remote shut in of compressor unit #3, and operations personnel were dispatched to the site. upon examination, there was a tubing failure on a relief valve inside the station. upon evaluation, operations determined that no overpressure event occurred. pressure was ~917psi when the prv lifted. it was noted that the nut and ferrule of the 1/8" stainless steel tubing broke at the pilot which, by design, caused a loss of pressure to the main valve dome thus triggering a fail-open condition (caused the relief valve to lift). the suspected failure is excessive vibration, so new tubing was installed in a configuration that alleviated the vibration issue. eqt production examined other stations with similar tubing configurations as the failed tubing and found them to be fully operational for many years and without vibration issues. eqt production believes that this was an isolated event and particular to the relief valve tubing at this specific relief valve at snapping turtle compressor station.

NAME: EASTERN GAS TRANSMISSION AND STORAGE, INC.
NARRATIVE: ON 10/1/2026 AT APPROXIMATELY 07:40, A GASKET ON THE DEHYDRATION SYSTEM HEAT EXCHANGER FAILED AND BEGAN LEAKING NATURAL GAS THROUGH THE ASSOCIATED FLANGE AT OAKFORD COMPRESSOR STATION WHICH IS LOCATED IN DELMONT, PENNSYLVANIA IN WESTMORELAND COUNTY AND IS MANNED 24 HOURS A DAY, 7 DAYS A WEEK. OAKFORD COMPRESSOR STATION WAS IN NORMAL OPERATION WITH AN OPERATING PRESSURE OF 762 PSIG AND A FLOW RATE OF 780,000 MSCF/D INJECTING NATURAL GAS INTO OAKFORD STORAGE WHEN THE GASKET FAILED. THE LEAKING NATURAL GAS SUBSEQUENTLY IGNITED AND CAUGHT FIRE. INITIAL INDICATION OF THE AUDIBLE NOISE CAUSED BY THE LEAKING NATURAL GAS WAS MADE BY OPERATIONS PERSONNEL AT THE FACILITY. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL NOTIFIED GAS CONTROL AT APPROXIMATELY 07:40 AND WERE DIRECTED BY GAS CONTROL TO INITIATE AN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF OAKFORD COMPRESSOR STATION. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL IMMEDIATELY INITIATED THE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN BY MANUALLY ACTIVATING EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN SYSTEM TRIGGERS AND THE BLOWDOWN OF THE FACILITY COMMENCED AT APPROXIMATELY 07:41 AND PROCEEDED UNTIL APPROXIMATELY 07:45. THE FIRE WAS EXTINGUISHED AT APPROXIMATELY 07:42. INITIAL NOTIFICATION (#1475032) WAS MADE TO THE NRC ON 10/1/2026 AT 08:34. WITH ALL OPERATIONS AT OAKFORD COMPRESSOR STATION SHUTDOWN, OAKFORD STORAGE WAS SHUT-IN AND THE DEHYDRATION SYSTEM WAS LOCKED OUT / TAGGED OUT TO ISOLATE IT FROM THE REST OF THE STATION PIPING. THE EVENT QUALIFIED AS AN INCIDENT AS A RESULT OF THE SHUT-IN OF OAKFORD STORAGE PER THE REQUIREMENTS OF §191.3(2). OAKFORD COMPRESSOR STATION, WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE LOCKED OUT / TAGGED OUT DEHYDRATION SYSTEM, WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE ON 10/1/2026 AT APPROXIMATELY 14:00 AND RESUMED INJECTING NATURAL GAS INTO OAKFORD STORAGE. FOLLOW UP NOTIFICATION (#1475163) WAS MADE TO THE NRC ON 10/2/2026 AT 11:39. THE VALVES IN THE HEAT AFFECTED ZONE WERE INSPECTED ON 10/2/2026. THE DEHYDRATION SYSTEM VALVE (DV801) WAS SENT OUT FOR REPAIRS AND TESTING, PASSED THE TESTING, AND WAS REINSTALLED. ALL OTHER VALVES WERE DETERMINED TO BE FIT-FOR-SERVICE. THE SHELL-AND-TUBE DEHYDRATION HEAT EXCHANGER WAS REMOVED AND HYDROSTATICALLY PRESSURE TESTED TO DETERMINE IF THERE WAS ANY POTENTIAL INTERNAL DAMAGE ON 10/3/2026. THE DEHYDRATION SYSTEM HEAT EXCHANGER INTERNAL TUBES WERE TESTED, FAILED TUBES WERE IDENTIFIED, AND FAILED TUBES WERE PLUGGED. THE DEHYDRATION SYSTEM HEAT EXCHANGER SHELL WAS HARDNESS TESTED AND IT WAS DETERMINED TO BE FIT-FOR-SERVICE. FITNESS-FOR-SERVICE EVALUATIONS (INCLUDING VISUAL ASSESSMENTS, IN-SITU HARDNESS TESTING, AND METALLURGICAL ASSESSMENTS) AND SUBSEQUENT ENGINEERING ANALYSES WERE CONDUCTED BY KIEFNER & ASSOCIATES ON PIPING AND EQUIPMENT WITHIN THE HEAT AFFECTED AREA TO ASSESS FOR POTENTIAL MATERIAL DEGRADATION FROM HEAT EXPOSURE STARTING ON 10/4/2026. THE FLANGE FACES ASSOCIATED WITH THE GASKET FAILURE WERE INSPECTED BY KIEFNER & ASSOCIATES TO VERIFY INTEGRITY AND ASSIST IN DETERMINING THE ROOT CAUSE ON 10/6/2026. THE DEHYDRATION SYSTEM HEAT EXCHANGER GASKET WAS REPLACED. THE DEHYDRATION SYSTEM CONTROL PANEL AND ASSOCIATED WIRING WERE REPLACED. THE DEHYDRATION SYSTEM WAS DETERMINED TO BE FIT-FOR-SERVICE AND THE LOCK OUT / TAG OUT WAS REMOVED ON 10/9/2026 AT APPROXIMATELY 14:00 AND THE DEHYDRATION SYSTEM WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE ON 10/11/2026 AT APPROXIMATELY 10:00. APPROXIMATELY 39.6 MCF OF NATURAL GAS LEAKED THROUGH THE FAILED GASKET AND ASSOCIATED FLANGE ON THE DEHYDRATION SYSTEM HEAT EXCHANGER AND WAS CONSUMED BY THE FIRE. APPROXIMATELY 2307 MCF OF NATURAL GAS WAS INTENTIONALLY BLOWN DOWN TO THE ATMOSPHERE DURING THE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN. THERE WERE NO INJURIES, FATALITIES, OR EVACUATION AND NO ACCOMPANYING LIQUIDS WERE RELEASED. EMERGENCY RESPONSE PERSONNEL WERE ENROUTE TO OAKFORD COMPRESSOR STATION, BUT WERE CALLED OFF BEFORE ARRIVING AS THE FIRE WAS ALREADY EXTINGUISHED.
